case: concurrent writers (no recorded case reaches it)
from: Go SELECTs view_prefs, merges in Go and UPDATEs, so concurrent writers can lose each other's keys
to: rust_settings_undo_delay_put locks the user row (FOR UPDATE) and merges in SQL in one transaction
reason: ARCH-028 statement-or-reducer rule: Go's handler is a read then a write, so Rust calls one reducer. Sequential results are identical (recorded); other numeric keys are not re-rounded through float64 because the document is merged as JSONB.

case: concurrent writers beyond the cap (no recorded case reaches it)
from: Go counts other rows outside the transaction, so two simultaneous new aliases can both pass at 99 rows
to: the reducer re-counts inside the transaction
reason: ARCH-028 statement-or-reducer rule: Go's handler is four statements. Rust still reads the count first so validation order is Go's; the reducer's count is the authoritative one.

case: Go process in a non-UTC time zone (no recorded case reaches it)
from: Go prints fmt %v of a pgx time.Time in the Go process's local zone (for example +0200 CEST)
to: Rust always prints UTC (2006-01-02 15:04:05.999999999 +0000 UTC), identical to Go whenever Go runs in UTC
reason: The local zone is host configuration, not data; the recorded oracle runs Go in UTC. A fixed UTC rendering keeps the wire value independent of where the Rust gateway runs.
